nativeAdaptations: Ratatui's cell buffer and Crossterm own the alternate screen; a transactional RAII session replaces OpenTUI renderer/root destruction while preserving teardown order on every return and error path.
The shipped CLI owns one revocable process-signal callback. Unix signal-hook covers the baseline's exact five-signal set; the Windows console backend covers Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Break, and close events.
Crossterm reports terminal read failures through the event loop, whose error return follows the same once-only shutdown path as an explicit disconnect callback.

The named TUI session adapter owns the modern authenticated broker client and producer, while terminal RAII remains session-independent. Workdeck's pre-existing direct review session remains active in parallel until its compatibility interface is separately retired.
Native highlight work is session-local rather than a global JavaScript worker; dropping the review explicitly disposes its logical worker queue and disconnects outstanding result receivers.
